subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Decaf: How It Works
description: A micro-lesson that makes Decaf: How It Works usable.

hook.text: Decaf coffee still contains about 3% of the original caffeine. True zero-caffeine coffee doesn't exist.

buildup.text: Swiss Water Process soaks green beans in water to dissolve caffeine, then filters it out with carbon.

discovery.text: Supercritical CO₂ extraction uses pressurized carbon dioxide as a selective solvent—targeting only caffeine.

twist.text: Early decaf methods used chemical solvents. Some critics still distrust decaf because of that history.

climax.text: Modern decaf quality has improved dramatically. Blind tastings show many people can't tell the difference.

punchline.text: Same bean, minus the buzz. Science got surprisingly good at this.

quiz.question: What does the Swiss Water Process use to remove caffeine?
